newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil under pressure in Europe after Wong report.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil under pressure in Europe after Wong report.

text.p: Palm oil sellers felt the pinch on Monday morning in Europe following the release of Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong's latest crop report which estimated June exports at 595,000 tonnes against 626,606 in May.

Wong also estimated palm oil output in June at 785,000 tonnes, against the 790,640 tonnes in May. He put stocks at the end of June at 795,000 tonnes, against the 711,8541 tonnes tallied by the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority at end-May.
Traders said the exports were very low and were more bad news for an already bearish market.
"This will certainly put the market back on the defensive with all eyes now on Chicago," said one trader.
News that Indonesia has restructured its palm oil export tax has been little impact on the market yet.
"People are still digesting the news from Indonesia," said another trader.
Little activity was reported on the soft or lauric oil markets where most players are awaiting the reopening of the U.S. markets following Friday's holiday.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was $2.50 to $5 lower after Aug/Sep traded at $517.50 and Oct/Dec at $520 a tonne cif.
RBD palm oil offers were $2.50 to $5 down while olein was $5 lower after Aug/Sep fetched $540 and $532.50 and Oct/Dec traded at $535 and $530 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Soft oils were around 0.50 guilders lower with an easier dollar allowing sellers to trim their prices.
Coconut oil was unchanged to $2.50 down while palmnkernel oil was $2.50 to $5 up in a neglected market.
